title: RTPSC Enhanced RBAC / ABAC Governance & Accuracy Policy
goals: Make authorization decisions explicit and testable.
Separate operational editing from approval, transmission, payout and governance.
Preserve financial and compliance evidence through non-destructive corrections.
Apply tenant, assignment, sensitivity, lifecycle and approval-state conditions to permissions.
Make analytics authoritative to recorded transactions rather than user-entered summaries.

abac: workspace_id must match authenticated tenant context.
Assigned-user restrictions apply unless elevated operational role is present.
Sensitive client data requires an authorized business purpose.
Closed or locked tax cases become read-only except controlled correction workflows.
Financial records use void, reverse, refund, adjustment or archive events instead of hard deletion.
Approval of a record created or materially changed by the approver is denied where segregation-of-duties applies.
decision_order: Record an audit event for material actions

action_definitions.update: Edit mutable fields on an existing record.
action_definitions.delete: Hard delete; default denied for compliance and financial records.
action_definitions.archive: Remove from active operational views without destroying history.
action_definitions.void: Invalidate a record while retaining evidence.
action_definitions.reverse: Create a compensating transaction for a prior transaction.
action_definitions.reject: Reject a workflow item with a reason.
action_definitions.transmit: Send an authorized tax or e-file transaction to an external gateway.
action_definitions.export: Extract data in an approved format subject to privacy and data-loss controls.
action_definitions.admin: Change configuration, role mappings or workspace-wide controls.

owner.responsibility: Enterprise governance, policy ownership, financial and security oversight
owner.permission_boundary: Full administrative control except actions prohibited by policy; audit history cannot be silently erased.

admin.permission_boundary: Can manage workspace operations; privileged self-approval is prohibited where segregation-of-duties applies.

ero.responsibility: ERO supervision, e-file operations, return oversight and practitioner governance
ero.permission_boundary: Can review, approve and transmit authorized returns; cannot bypass audit or alter immutable payment history.

practitioner.responsibility: Tax preparation, review, client communications and fee attribution
practitioner.permission_boundary: Can edit assigned tax work within authorization scope; cannot approve own privileged payout or erase financial history.

preparer.responsibility: Preparation support, data entry and document indexing
preparer.permission_boundary: Assigned-work scope only; no e-file transmission, payout approval, role administration or destructive financial actions.

collector.responsibility: Receivables, reminders, payment plans, collections and recovery
collector.permission_boundary: Can manage collection workflows and plans; cannot alter tax-return outcomes or independently write off balances above policy thresholds.

viewer.permission_boundary: Read-only unless an explicit additional grant exists.

rules: Never update a settled payment amount; use a reversal or refund event.
Never hard-delete an issued credential; revoke with an auditable reason.
Invoice balances must be reconciled from invoice lines and settled payment events.
Practitioner earnings are separate ledger records and must not be inferred from client balances.
Collection stages must be explainable from days past due and documented manual overrides.

analytics_rules: Every dashboard metric declares its source view or query, time window and unit.
AI-generated summaries reference underlying record IDs or source queries.
AI must never invent payment, refund, tax status, training completion or credential events.
Every KPI declares whether it is actual cash, accrual, pipeline or forecast.
